04 / THE IDEA BEHIND IT

A little knowledge.
A more informed search.

Uniform-Cost Search chooses the cheapest journey so far. A* adds a lower bound on the distance still to travel.

UCS: f(n) = g(n)
A*: f(n) = g(n) + h(n)

The custom heuristic combines three landmark distance bounds with a minimum-road-count bound. It is recalculated for your chosen goal.

TRI-ANCHOR + HOP HEURISTIC

A lower bound on
the road ahead.

h(n, goal) = max(landmark bounds, hop bound)

A landmark bound is the absolute difference between shortest road distances from a fixed landmark to the current city and to the goal. Landmarks: Arad, Neamt, and Eforie.

The hop bound is the fewest roads to the goal × 70 km, the shortest road in the network. Taking the maximum keeps the strongest of these lower bounds.

Why the shortest route is preserved

The triangle inequality makes each landmark bound no larger than the true remaining distance. Every route needs at least the minimum number of roads, each costing at least 70 km. Both bounds are consistent along every road; their maximum is also consistent. With positive road costs, A* therefore returns an optimal route.

This is a project-specific combination of established landmark and relaxed-problem techniques, not a claim to have invented a new search algorithm. Preprocessing costs and heuristic storage are disclosed in the comparison.

How the comparison is measured

Path cost: the sum of road distances. Expanded nodes: cities whose outgoing roads were examined; selecting the goal does not count as an expansion. Ties use alphabetical city order for both algorithms.

Runtime: median per-search duration across 15 batches of 100 runs, after 100 warm-up runs per algorithm. Execution order alternates by batch. Animation and trace recording are excluded. A* goal preparation and one-time landmark preparation are reported separately. These tiny searches are sensitive to timer precision, browser activity, and hardware; A* may not be faster.

Memory model: typed arrays for costs (160 B), parents (40 B), and explored flags (20 B), plus 8 B per peak frontier entry. A* additionally retains 480 B of landmark distances and 160 B of goal heuristic values. These figures exclude JavaScript object overhead, temporary preprocessing storage, map data, and visualization history. Peak stored cities and frontier size are also reported. This is a reproducible storage estimate, not a measurement of process RAM.
